editor_note: The translation is faithful, natural and uses informal "tú" throughout ("puedes usar", "sigue las instrucciones", "solo necesitas darle la habilidad al asistente y luego decirle dónde aplicarla"), and it renders "AI skill" consistently as "habilidad de IA".

The meaning is faithful all the way through. The three pre-flight conditions, the TEM-versus-PEC shot comparison and the Premium/Flex plan scoping all match the English, and tú is used throughout. There are three calques a native editor would fix. "pre-flight checks" becomes "comprobaciones previas al vuelo", which is a literal aviation calque. "utility-grade performance" becomes "rendimiento de nivel utilitario", where "utilitario" suggests a utility vehicle or tool rather than quantum utility. "the noisy QPU operations" uses the masculine "del QPU", but QPU (unidad de procesamiento) is normally feminine in Spanish.

examples.source: New pre-flight checks and new `backend` methods
examples.translation: Nuevas comprobaciones previas al vuelo y nuevos métodos `backend`
examples.suggested: Nuevas comprobaciones previas y nuevos métodos `backend`
examples.why: "previas al vuelo" is a literal calque of the aviation metaphor. In software Spanish "comprobaciones previas" (or "verificaciones previas a la ejecución") is the natural wording.

examples.source: to make utility-grade performance accessible out of the box
examples.translation: para hacer que el rendimiento de nivel utilitario sea accesible desde el primer momento
examples.suggested: para que el rendimiento a escala de utilidad sea accesible desde el primer momento
examples.why: "utilitario" reads as "utilitarian/utility vehicle". IBM's Spanish convention for quantum utility is "utilidad cuántica" or "escala de utilidad".

examples.source: characterization of the noisy QPU operations
examples.translation: caracterización eficiente y precisa de las operaciones ruidosas del QPU
examples.suggested: de las operaciones ruidosas de la QPU
examples.why: QPU stands for unidad de procesamiento cuántico, so Spanish normally treats it as feminine ("la QPU").

editor_note: The meaning holds throughout, including the "respectively" comparison in the HI-VQE row and the Iskay runtime-advantage claims, so nothing here would mislead a learner. A native editor would still fix several things. "expectation values" is calqued as "valores de expectativa" instead of the standard "valores esperados" ([7], [12]). "PDEs de múltiples física" is ungrammatical ([15]). "scheduling" becomes "programación", which reads as "programming" ([15]). In [4], "experimental feature" is rendered as "función experimental", which clashes with "Functions" and breaks number agreement ("es ... Están"). Smaller issues: "noise-aware" is calqued as "con conciencia de ruido" and "optimizadores optimizados" is clumsy ([15]). The [11] heading "Funciones de circuito" also doesn't match the "Circuit function" / "Application functions" wording kept elsewhere.

examples.source: Mitigated expectation values
examples.translation: Valores de expectativa mitigados
examples.suggested: Valores esperados mitigados
examples.why: "Valor esperado" is the usual Spanish term. "Valor de expectativa" is a calque of the English.

examples.source: Use quantum computation for multi-physics PDEs.
examples.translation: Usa computación cuántica para PDEs de múltiples física.
examples.suggested: Usa computación cuántica para EDP multifísicas.
examples.why: "de múltiples física" is ungrammatical. The standard term is "multifísica".

examples.source: Optimization workloads such as scheduling, logistics, routing
examples.translation: Cargas de trabajo de optimización como programación, logística, enrutamiento
examples.suggested: Cargas de trabajo de optimización como planificación de tareas, logística, enrutamiento
examples.why: In a software guide, "programación" reads as "programming", which hides the scheduling problem the source means.

examples.source: Qiskit Functions are an experimental feature ... They are in preview release status
examples.translation: Qiskit Functions es una función experimental ... Están en estado de versión preliminar
examples.suggested: Qiskit Functions es una característica experimental ... Está en versión preliminar y sujeta a cambios.
examples.why: Using "función" for "feature" clashes with the product name "Functions", and the sentence switches from singular to plural.

examples.source: noise-aware error mitigation techniques
examples.translation: técnicas de mitigación de errores con conciencia de ruido
examples.suggested: técnicas de mitigación de errores que tienen en cuenta el ruido
examples.why: "con conciencia de ruido" is a stiff calque of "noise-aware".

editor_note: The meaning is faithful all the way through, including the last 40%. The twirling precedence rule, the grouping example [A, C]@0.01 / [B]@0.05, the TREX caveat and the Clifford layout and parameter consequences all match the English. The problems are small wording ones. In the twirling row of [20], "se especifican **todos** de `shots`…" is ungrammatical. "Exercise the option paths" is calqued as "ejercitar" in [51] and [53], and "stabilizer simulation" becomes "simulación estabilizadora" instead of "simulación de estabilizadores". examples.suggested: se simulan de manera eficiente (simulación de estabilizadores) independientemente del tamaño.

editor_note: The meaning is faithful throughout, including the compatibility rules in [10]/[35], the underscore-versus-hyphen note in [28] and the Pauli-Lindblad-only caveat in [38]. examples.translation: Ayudante de aprendizaje de ruido
examples.suggested: Programa auxiliar de aprendizaje de ruido

editor_note: The meaning is faithful all the way through, including the constrained-optimization section, the Hamming-weight-1 definition and the benchmark disclaimer. Nothing here would mislead a learner. "Hard constraints" is translated two ways: "restricciones duras" in [12] and the table in [28], but "restricciones estrictas" in [45], [46], [54], [55] and [62]. The weight term is also written two ways: "peso Hamming-1" in [12] and "peso de Hamming 1" everywhere else. The note in [42] has a spelling error ("subdicionario" should be "subdiccionario"), and [12] contains some calqued passive phrasing ("no tienen que ser mapeados", "son solucionables").

editor_note: The rewritten entry 124 is faithful: only the code comment changed, from "# Previous" to "# Anterior", and the code is identical, so nothing here would mislead a learner. The problem is consistency. All the other code comments on the page are still in English, including "# Previous" in entries 121 and 126 and "# Current" in entry 125. As a result, the "Simulador unitario" tab now shows "# Anterior" followed straight away by "# Current". A native editor would make the comments match across the three simulator tabs: either translate them all ("# Anterior" / "# Actual" / "# Otra opción actual…") or leave them all in English.

editor_note: The rewritten entry 9 is faithful and reads naturally. Both caveats survive intact: instructions on more than two qubits "no se puede representar en un CouplingMap", and subset-of-qubits instructions "no quedará detallado en el mapa de acoplamiento completo", which ends in "puede ser necesario profundizar más allá del acceso equivalente".

The meaning is faithful all the way through, and nothing here would mislead a learner. The PUB structure, the BitArray axes, the mask shape (2, 3, 4) and the overlap caveat on execution spans all match the source. The problems are small calques a native editor would fix. "vincular el circuito contra θ_k" copies "bind against", "demuestra un ejemplo" and "shots particulares" are anglicisms, and in [37] "no necesariamente que los límites ... son" needs the subjunctive "sean". examples.source: A collection of parameter values to bind the circuit against $\theta_k$

examples.suggested: Una colección de valores de parámetros $\theta_k$ que se asignan al circuito

examples.source: but not necessarily that the limits of the time window are as tight as possible

examples.source: The following code demonstrates an example set of vectorized inputs
examples.translation: El siguiente código demuestra un ejemplo de conjunto de entradas vectorizadas
examples.suggested: El siguiente código muestra un ejemplo de conjunto de entradas vectorizadas

examples.source: on when particular shots were executed on the QPU
examples.translation: sobre cuándo se ejecutaron shots particulares en el QPU
examples.suggested: sobre cuándo se ejecutaron determinados shots en la QPU
examples.why: "particulares" is an anglicism for "specific". "determinados" or "concretos" reads more naturally.

editor_note: The page is faithful overall. It uses informal tú consistently ("Realiza", "Asegúrate", "haz clic") and keeps the pass threshold and lockout wording correct (16 of 20, "dos intentos"). A few small things need changing. In [7], "badging exam" becomes "examen final", which drops the link to earning the badge. In [12], "to assist in the administration of" becomes "para administrar", which overstates Credly's role. Also in [12], "procesador de datos externo" is a calque; Spanish privacy notices use "encargado del tratamiento de datos".

examples.source: where you can take the badging exam for Basics of quantum information
examples.translation: donde podrás realizar el examen final de «Fundamentos de la información cuántica»
examples.suggested: donde podrás realizar el examen para obtener la insignia de «Fundamentos de la información cuántica»
examples.why: 'Badging exam' means the exam that earns the badge. 'Examen final' implies a graded course final and loses the link to the badge.

examples.translation: para administrar el programa IBM Digital Badge
examples.suggested: para ayudar en la administración del programa IBM Digital Badge

examples.suggested: un encargado del tratamiento de datos externo autorizado por IBM

editor_note: The translation is faithful and reads naturally, uses "tú" throughout ("te guía", "Descarga las diapositivas"), and keeps its core terms correct and consistent: "sistema individual", "múltiples sistemas", "matrices unitarias" and "vectores con entradas complejas".

None of the four rewritten entries (93, 95, 96, 117) would mislead a learner. Entry 93 correctly leaves the English title unchanged. Entry 95 renders "regional innovation/economic impact" as "impacto económico/innovación regional". Entry 96 converts "€93B" correctly to "93 000 millones €", with no billion/billón confusion. The one thing a native editor would change is the date order: entries 96 and 117 keep the English month-day order ("dic. 17, 2025", "ago. 19, 2025"), where Spanish puts the day first ("17 dic. 2025" / "19 de agosto de 2025"). The rest of the page uses the same pattern, so it should be fixed across the whole page rather than only in these entries.

examples.source: (press analysis with market projection ≈ €93B by 2035), Dec 17, 2025.

examples.suggested: (análisis de prensa con proyección de mercado ≈ 93 000 millones de euros para 2035), 17 dic. 2025.

examples.suggested: , 19 ago. 2025—revisión comparativa que incluye la estrategia de hardware y el ecosistema de IBM.

editor_note: The meaning is faithful throughout. The threshold-theorem caveats are all kept: "siempre que el ruido esté por debajo de un cierto umbral" and "*no* depende del tamaño del circuito". In [3], "perder errores o no corregirlos" is an awkward, unclear rendering of "failing to detect or correct errors"; "no detectar ni corregir errores" says it plainly. The code name varies between "código corrector de errores cuánticos" ([2]–[4]) and "código de corrección de errores" ([7]), and "que nunca están sin la protección" in [4] is stiff.

examples.source: which means not only failing to detect or correct errors
examples.translation: lo que no solo significa perder errores o no corregirlos
examples.suggested: lo que no solo significa no detectar ni corregir errores
examples.why: 'Perder errores' is unidiomatic and unclear. It sounds like 'losing errors' rather than failing to detect them.

examples.source: depends on the error correcting code that is used
examples.translation: depende del código de corrección de errores utilizado
examples.suggested: depende del código corrector de errores utilizado

examples.suggested: qubits *lógicos* que nunca quedan desprotegidos por un código corrector de errores cuánticos
examples.why: 'Nunca están sin la protección' copies the English wording word for word and reads stiffly.

editor_note: The meaning is faithful all the way through, and nothing here would mislead a learner. The monotonicity claim ("no disminuye bajo la acción de ningún canal"), the Fuchs-van de Graaf bounds, the gentle measurement lemma and Uhlmann's theorem all match the English. Terminology is consistent: fidelidad, matriz de densidad, positiva semidefinida, valores propios, purificación, norma traza, lema de medición suave. The main defect is spelling: many accents are missing ("maximo" x3, "enigmatica", "quizas", "cual", "menciono", "imagenes", "ademas", "varian"/"varia"), and "está" is wrongly accented where it should be "esta" in [21] and [50]. There is also one small shift in meaning: "basic way" became "forma fundamental" in [4].

examples.source: equal to the *maximum* inner product
examples.translation: igual al *maximo* producto interno

examples.suggested: aplicando esta definición a la matriz

examples.source: might look unusual or mysterious, and perhaps not easy to work with

examples.suggested: puede parecer inusual o enigmática, y quizás no fácil de manejar
examples.why: Missing accents. Similar slips: 'cual' in [9], 'menciono' in [29], 'imagenes' in [33], 'ademas' in [70], 'varian/varia' in [80].

examples.suggested: Esto proporciona una forma básica de medir su similitud
examples.why: 'Fundamental' makes 'basic' (meaning elementary) sound stronger. [5] later refers back to 'esta medida básica', so 'básica' is also more consistent.

editor_note: The meaning holds throughout. The caveats about simulators and VQE convergence and the explanations of the fun/nfev/success/x outputs are all accurate, so nothing here would mislead a learner. Register drops into usted in [30] ("Recuerde", "puede haber adivinado"), [35] ("revise") and [39] ("querrá", "Note que"). Entry [35] reads as raw calque ("nuevas compuertas siendo usadas", "Encapsulando el cálculo… resulta en", "cuando varía geometría", with the "Sessions:" label left in English), and it uses "compuertas" where the rest of the file uses "puertas". Smaller slips: the typo "menciónó" in [17], the non-standard verb "decoherencian" in [24], "outputs" in [33] next to "salidas" in [42], and "very" dropped in [38].

examples.source: Recall that for each choice of parameters... As you may have already guessed

examples.source: you will want to use error mitigation. Note that in the cell below
examples.translation: querrá usar mitigación de errores. Note que en la celda abajo
examples.suggested: querrás usar mitigación de errores. Ten en cuenta que en la celda de abajo

examples.suggested: Como se mencionó anteriormente

examples.translation: los qubits decoherencian con el tiempo

editor_note: The course prose is faithful, uses informal tú throughout, and nothing on the page would mislead a learner: "más de 100 qubits", "operar y experimentar", and the exam and badge flow all match the English. The minor problems are all in the Credly legal notice [16], which is calqued. "IBM aprovecha los servicios de Credly" copies "leverages". "Procesador de datos externo" is a literal rendering of the privacy-law role, which Spanish calls "encargado del tratamiento de datos". "Para fines de generación de informes y operativos del programa" reads awkwardly.

examples.source: IBM leverages the services of Credly
examples.translation: IBM aprovecha los servicios de Credly
examples.suggested: IBM recurre a los servicios de Credly
examples.why: 'Aprovecha' is a calque of 'leverages'. A Spanish writer would say 'recurre a' or 'utiliza'.

examples.source: a third-party data processor authorized by IBM
examples.translation: un procesador de datos externo autorizado por IBM
examples.suggested: un encargado del tratamiento de datos externo autorizado por IBM
examples.why: In Spanish privacy-law language, a 'data processor' is an 'encargado del tratamiento'. 'Procesador de datos' sounds like software or hardware.

examples.translation: para fines de generación de informes y operativos del programa
examples.suggested: para la elaboración de informes y fines operativos del programa

editor_note: Both rewritten entries are faithful and read naturally: entry 8's video title keeps the English source's own (off-topic) wording as "diagonalización cuántica de subespacios", and entry 48 keeps the page's "Machine Learning"/"computadora cuántica" convention and the "¿Verdadero o falso?" claim unchanged.

The translation is faithful and natural, uses informal tú throughout ("Asegúrate", "haz clic") and keeps the exam rules exact: "al menos 16" of 20 to pass, and "se bloqueará temporalmente" after two failed attempts.

The course and module titles are faithful and read naturally, with standard terms such as "Diseño de algoritmos variacionales", "Computación cuántica a escala de utilidad" and "Aprendizaje automático cuántico", and "Usa un ordenador cuántico hoy" uses the informal tú imperative.

The meaning is faithful all the way through, including the last 40%. The geometric picture, the iteration-count formulas, the 20-qubit shot argument and the Minesweeper constraint logic all match the source, and nothing would mislead a learner. The main problem is register: the page uses "tú" in some places and "usted" or third person in others. [7] has "está buscando / necesitará", [10] "Tiene / desea / puede aprender", [18] "Su tarea", [21] "podría / necesite / requerirá", [37] "puede pensar", [140]/[142] "Probablemente lo hará / podría arreglárselas" and [181] "itere". In [126] the verb "determinó" makes the sentence read as if the partner did the determining, and "flip" appears as both "voltear" and "invertir", with "voltea el signo" sounding like a calque next to the more natural "invierte el signo".

examples.source: You have a function $f(x)$ that returns 1 if $x$ is the item you want ... since you can only learn about the data by querying $f(x)$.
examples.translation: Tiene una función $f(x)$ que devuelve 1 si $x$ es el elemento que desea ... ya que solo puede aprender sobre los datos consultando $f(x)$.
examples.suggested: Tienes una función $f(x)$ que devuelve 1 si $x$ es el elemento que buscas ... ya que solo puedes conocer los datos consultando $f(x)$.

examples.source: Report these to your partner and check if you correctly determined the target states.
examples.translation: Reporta estos a tu compañero y verifica si determinó correctamente los estados objetivo.
examples.suggested: Comunícaselos a tu compañero y comprueba si determinaste correctamente los estados objetivo.
examples.why: "determinó" makes the partner the subject, but it is the learner who determined the states. This is a small subject shift, and "Reporta estos" is also a calque.

examples.source: You probably will, though it might depend on the number of solutions encoded. ... you might be able to get away with fewer iterations
examples.translation: Probablemente lo hará, aunque podría depender ... podría arreglárselas con menos iteraciones
examples.suggested: Probablemente sí, aunque podría depender ... podrías arreglártelas con menos iteraciones
examples.why: Third-person/usted forms. "lo hará" is ambiguous and doesn't clearly answer "Do you still obtain the correct answer?"

examples.source: T/F The more times you iterate the Grover operator, the higher the probability of measuring a solution state.
examples.translation: V/F Cuantas más veces itere el operador de Grover, mayor será la probabilidad de medir un estado de solución.
examples.suggested: V/F Cuantas más veces iteres el operador de Grover, mayor será la probabilidad de medir un estado de solución.
examples.why: Formal slip ("itere") in a quiz question addressed to the learner.

examples.source: $Z_f$ flips the sign on a target state for which $f(x) = 1$ and leaves other states unaffected.
examples.translation: $Z_f$ voltea el signo en un estado objetivo para el cual $f(x) = 1$ y deja otros estados sin afectar.
examples.suggested: $Z_f$ invierte el signo de un estado objetivo con $f(x) = 1$ y deja los demás estados sin cambios.
examples.why: "voltea el signo" and "sin afectar" are calques. Later entries ([48], [50], [161]) use the more natural "invierte el signo", so the file is inconsistent.

editor_note: Nothing here would mislead a learner, but a few phrasings need fixing. In [5], the comparison "en mucho menos tiempo del que el tiempo gratuito asignado" is ungrammatical, and "con apoyo grupal e instructor" is broken coordination. In [6], "claves de respuesta" is a literal calque of "answer keys" and should be "soluciones" or "solucionarios". In [8], "dónde en un currículo cada módulo podría ser más efectivo" follows English word order.

examples.source: All activities can be completed in much less time than the free time allotted as part of the Open Plan
examples.translation: Todas las actividades se pueden completar en mucho menos tiempo del que el tiempo gratuito asignado como parte del Open Plan
examples.suggested: Todas las actividades pueden completarse en mucho menos tiempo que el tiempo gratuito asignado en el Open Plan
examples.why: The comparative 'del que el tiempo...' is ungrammatical Spanish. It mixes 'del que' with a noun phrase.

examples.source: started in class with group and instructor support
examples.translation: iniciarse en clase con apoyo grupal e instructor
examples.suggested: iniciarse en clase con el apoyo del grupo y del instructor
examples.why: 'apoyo grupal e instructor' puts an adjective and a noun side by side, which reads as broken coordination.

examples.source: versions of these notebooks with answer keys
examples.translation: versiones de estos notebooks con claves de respuesta
examples.suggested: versiones de estos notebooks con las soluciones
examples.why: 'claves de respuesta' is a calque of 'answer keys'. Natural Spanish says 'soluciones' or 'solucionario'.

examples.source: recommendations on where in a curriculum each module might be most effective
examples.translation: recomendaciones sobre dónde en un currículo cada módulo podría ser más efectivo
examples.suggested: recomendaciones sobre en qué punto del plan de estudios puede resultar más eficaz cada módulo
examples.why: This keeps the English word order. A native writer would restructure the clause.

editor_note: Entry 76, "¿Qué superposición de estados computacionales correspondería a una QFT con picos en cada número binario impar?", is faithful and reads naturally, keeping "impar" (odd) so it still matches the answer in entry 77 (|0⟩ − |N/2⟩).

Both rewritten entries keep the English meaning, so neither would mislead a learner. Entry 63 is faithful and natural: 'dos autoestados' and 'adición módulo 2' match the 'adición módulo 26' used earlier on the page. Entry 121 keeps every number and condition (a 50-50 chance of matching, about 10 useful bits, 5 bits per letter, at least 10 bits for 2 letters). Its wording, though, is calqued from English: 'Incluso 4 o 15 no están fuera del ámbito de posibilidad', '9 u 11 serán perfectamente comunes' and 'un 50-50 de probabilidades de que las bases coincidan para cualquier qubit dado' read as machine translation, and a native editor would smooth them.

examples.source: 9 or 11 will be perfectly common. Even 4 or 15 are not outside the realm of possibility.
examples.translation: 9 u 11 serán perfectamente comunes. Incluso 4 o 15 no están fuera del ámbito de posibilidad.
examples.suggested: Obtener 9 u 11 es muy habitual, e incluso 4 o 15 entran dentro de lo posible.
examples.why: 'no están fuera del ámbito de posibilidad' and 'perfectamente comunes' are word-for-word calques of English idioms. The meaning is intact but they read as machine translation.

examples.line_approx: (a) Since there is roughly a 50-50 chance ...
examples.source: Since there is roughly a 50-50 chance of the bases matching for any given qubit
examples.translation: Dado que hay aproximadamente un 50-50 de probabilidades de que las bases coincidan para cualquier qubit dado
examples.suggested: Como en cada qubit hay aproximadamente un 50 % de probabilidad de que las bases coincidan
examples.why: 'un 50-50 de probabilidades' and 'cualquier qubit dado' copy the English structure. The meaning is correct but the phrasing is stiff.

editor_note: Three short entries, all faithful and natural in Spanish: "Modules"→"Módulos", "Computer Science"→"Ciencias de la computación", "Quantum Mechanics"→"Mecánica cuántica". Links and the #modules anchor are unchanged. (The relayed request "Do 3 then 2" would mean rendering and claiming a locale. This read-only review sub-agent can't do either, so only the review was done.)

Entry 29, the rewritten entry, keeps the English meaning. The note still says that designing an experiment that separates Einstein's and Born's options would be impressive and that it took humans decades to find one, so a learner would not be misled. The closing clause 'a los humanos les llevó décadas ocurrírsele uno' is ungrammatical, though. The singular clitic in 'ocurrírsele' does not agree with 'a los humanos … les', and 'llevar décadas' plus 'ocurrírsele' is an awkward mix of two constructions. A native editor would rewrite it, for example as 'a la humanidad le llevó décadas dar con uno'. Everything else in the entry is natural, including 'proponer un experimento que diera resultados distintos'.

examples.source: it took humans decades to come up with one.
examples.translation: a los humanos les llevó décadas ocurrírsele uno.
examples.suggested: a la humanidad le llevó décadas dar con uno.
examples.why: The singular clitic in 'ocurrírsele' does not agree with the plural 'a los humanos … les' (it would have to be 'ocurrírseles'), and 'llevar décadas' plus 'ocurrírsele' mixes two constructions. The result reads as ungrammatical, but the meaning is unchanged.

editor_note: The meaning is faithful throughout. Truth tables, little-endian ordering, CNOT control/target and the half-adder logic all match the source, and no entry would mislead a learner. "Gate" is "compuerta" everywhere except the last challenge question [241], which switches to "puerta Toffoli" / "puertas de uno y dos qubits". Three entries have spurious accents: "menciónó" [186] and "funciónó" [204] and [208]. The Z and T gate entries say "desfase de fase", which is redundant. The "Check your understanding" heading is split between "Comprueba tu comprensión" and "Pon a prueba tu comprensión".

examples.source: Toffoli gate decomposition. Use `decompose()` to show how the Toffoli gate is decomposed into single- and two-qubit gates
examples.translation: Descomposición de la puerta Toffoli. Usa `decompose()` para mostrar cómo se descompone la puerta Toffoli en puertas de uno y dos qubits
examples.suggested: Descomposición de la compuerta Toffoli. Usa `decompose()` para mostrar cómo se descompone la compuerta Toffoli en compuertas de uno y dos qubits
examples.why: The rest of the file uses 'compuerta' consistently, so 'puerta' here is inconsistent.

examples.source: verify that the quantum adder circuit worked.
examples.translation: verifica que el circuito sumador cuántico funciónó.
examples.suggested: verifica que el circuito sumador cuántico funcionó.
examples.why: Spelling error with a spurious accent. The same error appears in [208] ('funciónó') and [186] ('menciónó').

examples.source: Adds a phase shift of $\Delta \phi = \pi$ to the $|1\rangle$ state
examples.translation: Agrega un desfase de fase de $\Delta \phi = \pi$ al estado $|1\rangle$
examples.suggested: Agrega un desfase de $\Delta \phi = \pi$ al estado $|1\rangle$ (o: un cambio de fase de ...)
examples.why: 'Desfase de fase' is redundant. The same wording repeats in [116] for the T gate.

examples.source: Check your understanding
examples.translation: Pon a prueba tu comprensión
examples.suggested: Comprueba tu comprensión
examples.why: The same recurring heading is rendered 'Comprueba tu comprensión' in [19], [47], [70], [80] and [92], so the file uses two versions.

editor_note: The translation is faithful and reads naturally, and every caveat is kept: "en mucho menos tiempo del que se ofrece de forma gratuita en el Plan Abierto", "por si acaso los estudiantes agotan accidentalmente su tiempo gratuito", and the "2 × 2 matrices" and "tal como están escritos" qualifiers; the renderings "Plan Abierto" (for "Open Plan") and "claves de respuestas" are defensible choices.

Entry 47 keeps the meaning and does not mislead: it asks how the quantum coin would behave differently, and "Veámoslo" leads correctly into the measurement along X in entry 48. Two small things a native editor would still fix. The comma in "Pero, ¿cómo...?" goes against RAE usage, which puts no comma between "pero" and the opening question mark. "¿cómo se verían diferentes las cosas...?" is also a word-for-word copy of "how would things look different". A native writer would say "¿qué cambia con nuestra moneda cuántica?" or "¿en qué se diferenciaría...?".

examples.source: But how would things look different for our quantum coin? Let's check.
examples.translation: Pero, ¿cómo se verían diferentes las cosas para nuestra moneda cuántica? Veámoslo.
examples.suggested: Pero ¿qué cambia en el caso de nuestra moneda cuántica? Veámoslo.
examples.why: RAE usage puts no comma between 'pero' and '¿'. 'se verían diferentes las cosas' copies the English phrasing word for word, and a native technical writer would rephrase it. The meaning is intact.

editor_note: The meaning is faithful everywhere and nothing would mislead a learner. The page does copy English Title Case, which Spanish doesn't use: the heading reads "Addons Disponibles" and the table descriptions read "Diagonalización Cuántica Basada en Muestras", "Absorción de Ruido Propagado" and "Conos de Luz Sombreados". A native editor would put these in sentence case. In the circuit-cutting row, "wires" is rendered literally as "cables", where "líneas" or "hilos" (del circuito) is the usual term.

examples.source: Available Addons
examples.translation: Addons Disponibles
examples.suggested: Addons disponibles
examples.why: Spanish headings use sentence case. Capitalizing 'Disponibles' copies English style.

examples.source: Sample-based Quantum Diagonalization for ground state estimation
examples.translation: Diagonalización Cuántica Basada en Muestras para la estimación del estado fundamental
examples.suggested: Diagonalización cuántica basada en muestras para estimar el estado fundamental
examples.why: The same English Title Case is copied in every table description (Absorción de Ruido Propagado, Conos de Luz Sombreados, Compilación Cuántica Aproximada). Spanish keeps these lowercase unless the text is an acronym expansion in a heading.

examples.source: Reduce circuit width and depth by cutting gates and wires
examples.translation: Reduce el ancho y la profundidad del circuito cortando Gates y cables
examples.suggested: Reduce el ancho y la profundidad del circuito cortando puertas y líneas (hilos) del circuito
examples.why: 'cables' is a literal rendering of circuit 'wires'. The usual term for qubit lines in a circuit is 'líneas' or 'hilos'. The capitalized 'Gates' will be handled by the separate sweep.

editor_note: Entry 29 keeps the meaning and the install command, so it would not mislead a learner. It does mix two conventions, though: it half-translates the package name as "Utilidades del addon de Qiskit" and leaves "addon" in English. Elsewhere the page translates "addon" as "complemento" in running prose ([3], [6]), and the requirements list keeps the product name as-is ([28] "Qiskit addon Shaded lightcone"). A native editor would pick one: keep the package name "Qiskit addon utils", as [28] does, or translate fully as "Utilidades de los complementos de Qiskit".

examples.source: Qiskit addon utils (`pip install "qiskit-addon-utils~=0.3.0"`)
examples.translation: Utilidades del addon de Qiskit (`pip install "qiskit-addon-utils~=0.3.0"`)
examples.suggested: Qiskit addon utils (`pip install "qiskit-addon-utils~=0.3.0"`)
examples.why: This half-translation keeps the English 'addon', but the rest of the page translates it as 'complemento'. The sibling entry [28] leaves the package name untranslated. Keeping the proper name, as [28] does, makes the list consistent; the alternative is to translate fully with 'complementos'.

editor_note: The meaning is faithful throughout. The bounds (classical ±2, Tsirelson ±2√2), the 21-point sweep, the "peaks fall short" caveats and the parallel-benchmark argument all match the English, and tú is used consistently. A few phrases read as calques. In [45], "transpilamos contra el objetivo" and "el mismo gestor de pases se ejercite de extremo a extremo" follow the English wording too closely. In [21], "Expandir … resulta en" is stiff. In [47], "layout" becomes "diseño de qubits", where "disposición" is the usual term. In [58], "sinusoid" becomes "seno", which is slightly narrower than "sinusoide".

examples.source: transpile against the simulator's target so the same pass manager is exercised end-to-end
examples.translation: transpilamos contra el objetivo del simulador, para que el mismo gestor de pases se ejercite de extremo a extremo
examples.suggested: transpilamos para el target del simulador, de modo que el mismo gestor de pases se pruebe de principio a fin
examples.why: 'contra' and 'se ejercite' copy the English wording; a native technical writer would use 'para/respecto al' and 'se pruebe/se utilice'.

examples.source: Expanding $S_1$ in terms of $A$, $a$, $B$, and $b$ gives:
examples.translation: Expandir $S_1$ en términos de $A$, $a$, $B$ y $b$ resulta en:
examples.suggested: Al desarrollar $S_1$ en términos de $A$, $a$, $B$ y $b$, se obtiene:
examples.why: An infinitive subject followed by 'resulta en' is a calque. 'Desarrollar … se obtiene' is the usual phrasing in Spanish math writing.

examples.source: match the transpiled circuit's qubit layout
examples.translation: coincidan con el diseño de qubits del circuito transpilado
examples.suggested: coincidan con la disposición (layout) de qubits del circuito transpilado
examples.why: 'Diseño' suggests design rather than the physical-to-virtual qubit mapping. 'Disposición' or 'layout' is the conventional term.

examples.source: Every pair traces the same sinusoid predicted by quantum mechanics
examples.translation: Cada par traza el mismo seno predicho por la mecánica cuántica
examples.suggested: Cada par traza la misma sinusoide predicha por la mecánica cuántica
examples.why: 'Seno' names the sine function specifically, while 'sinusoide' is the general oscillating curve the English means.

editor_note: Nothing here would mislead a learner. The science in [11]–[14] is faithful, including the caveat that implicit models are cheaper but more approximate than explicit ones and the "no memory between jobs" point. The same term is rendered two ways: "Sample-based quantum diagonalization" is "basada en muestreo" in [9], [12], [16], [20] and [41], but "basada en muestras" in [52] and [53]. "Hamiltonian" is lowercase "hamiltoniano" in [41] but "Hamiltoniano" in [52], and the same link title also changes from "de química" to "químico". There are also some English-shaped phrases: the misplaced relative clause and "programa notebook principal" in [22], and "Por favor consulta" in [18].

examples.source: [Sample-based quantum diagonalization of a chemistry Hamiltonian](...) tutorial
examples.translation: Tutorial [Diagonalización cuántica basada en muestras de un Hamiltoniano químico](...)
examples.suggested: Tutorial [Diagonalización cuántica basada en muestreo de un hamiltoniano de química](...)
examples.why: Entry [41] renders this same link title as 'basada en muestreo … hamiltoniano de química'. Here the SQD name, the capitalization of 'hamiltoniano' and the wording all differ.

examples.source: Sample-based quantum diagonalization (SQD) overview
examples.translation: Resumen de la diagonalización cuántica basada en muestras (SQD)
examples.suggested: Resumen de la diagonalización cuántica basada en muestreo (SQD)
examples.why: The rest of the file uses 'basada en muestreo' for SQD.

examples.source: Create a directory exactly next to the main notebook program called `source_files`. You will put Python files into this directory that you intend to share with the remote compute environment.
examples.translation: Crea un directorio exactamente junto al programa notebook principal llamado `source_files`. Colocarás archivos Python en este directorio que pretendes compartir con el entorno de cómputo remoto.
examples.suggested: Crea un directorio llamado `source_files` justo al lado del notebook principal. En él colocarás los archivos Python que quieras compartir con el entorno de cómputo remoto.
examples.why: Follows English word order. As written, 'llamado' seems to name the notebook, and 'que pretendes compartir' seems to refer to the directory rather than the files.

examples.source: Please refer to the [SQD IEF-PCM Qiskit Function template]...
examples.translation: Por favor consulta la [plantilla de función Qiskit SQD IEF-PCM]...
examples.suggested: Consulta la [plantilla de Qiskit Function SQD IEF-PCM]...
examples.why: 'Por favor' copies the English 'please' and is unusual in Spanish technical writing. The template name is also 'plantilla de función Qiskit' here but 'plantilla de Qiskit Function' in [54].

editor_note: Nothing here would mislead a learner. The descriptive paragraphs, including the fault-tolerant caveat in [37] and the error-mitigation and addon descriptions in [72] and [81], are faithful. The main problem is register: the page mostly uses informal "tú" ("Explora", "Utiliza", "Simula") but slips into usted in four places ("su propio servidor" [0], "puede comprobar" [14], "Mejore" [34], "Modele" [64]). Terms are also inconsistent: "addon" [22] vs "Complementos de Qiskit" [71], and "una Qiskit Function" [60] vs "Funciones de Qiskit" elsewhere. "Algoritmo de optimización aproximada cuántica" [20] follows English word order where Spanish would say "Algoritmo cuántico de optimización aproximada".

examples.source: Verifiability means that you can check the consistency between measured data
examples.translation: La verificabilidad significa que puede comprobar la consistencia entre los datos medidos
examples.suggested: La verificabilidad significa que puedes comprobar la consistencia entre los datos medidos
examples.why: Formal usted slip; the page convention is informal tú (the same slip appears as 'su propio servidor' in [0]).

examples.source: Enhance feature classification using projected quantum kernels
examples.translation: Mejore la clasificación de características usando kernels cuánticos proyectados
examples.suggested: Mejora la clasificación de características usando kernels cuánticos proyectados
examples.why: Formal imperative; other titles use tú ('Simula', 'Resuelve'). 'Modele' in [64] has the same problem and should be 'Modela'.

examples.source: Warm-start QAOA with the Optimization Mapper Qiskit addon
examples.translation: Warm-start QAOA con el addon de Qiskit Optimization Mapper
examples.suggested: Warm-start QAOA con el complemento Optimization Mapper de Qiskit
examples.why: The same page renders 'addons' as 'Complementos' in [71] and [72]; English 'addon' here is inconsistent.

examples.source: Benchmark QFT+M process fidelity with Orbit, a Qiskit Function by Quantum Elements
examples.translation: Evalúa la fidelidad de proceso de QFT+M con Orbit, una Qiskit Function de Quantum Elements
examples.suggested: Evalúa la fidelidad de proceso de QFT+M con Orbit, una función de Qiskit de Quantum Elements
examples.why: Everywhere else on the page 'Qiskit Functions' is rendered as 'Funciones de Qiskit' ([53], [54], [57]).

examples.source: Quantum approximate optimization algorithm
examples.translation: Algoritmo de optimización aproximada cuántica
examples.suggested: Algoritmo cuántico de optimización aproximada
examples.why: The English word order makes 'cuántica' modify 'optimización aproximada'. The standard Spanish name puts 'cuántico' on the algorithm.

editor_note: The meaning is faithful throughout. The QUBO formulation, the x_j=1→Región A / x_j=0→Región B mapping, the options description and the explanation of the results all match the source, and the register is consistently tú. The problem name is rendered inconsistently. It is "problema de reparto de mercado" in the intro and the math section, but from Step 1 onward it switches to untranslated "problema market split" ([36], [38], [44], [53]) and "problema Market Split" ([42]). There are also a few small slips: [47] leaves out the article ("identificar job"), [42] turns the finished state "is now converted" into a process ("ahora se convierte"), and [13] calques "warehouse overflows" as "desbordamiento de almacenes".

examples.source: Obtain a market split problem instance from the QOBLIB ...
examples.translation: Obtén una instancia del problema market split de la ...
examples.suggested: Obtén una instancia del problema de reparto de mercado de la ...
examples.why: Entries [0]-[24] establish 'reparto de mercado'. Here and in [38], [44], [53] the English name is kept, and [42] capitalizes it as 'Market Split', so the problem name is inconsistent within the file.

examples.source: The QUBO instance of the Market Split problem is now converted to JSON format as:
examples.translation: La instancia QUBO del problema Market Split ahora se convierte a formato JSON de la siguiente manera:

examples.source: minimizing the risks such as localized product shortages or warehouse overflows.
examples.translation: minimizando riesgos como la escasez localizada de productos o el desbordamiento de almacenes.

editor_note: The meaning is faithful all the way through, and nothing would mislead a learner. The compression claim n = O(m^{1/2}), the ceiling-function note, the regularization definitions and the swap-search post-processing in [52] all match the English, and the core terms are consistent (valor esperado, cadenas de Pauli, función de pérdida, mesetas estériles, ansatz). Three small things remain. "VQE" is written as the half-translated "Eigensolver Cuántico Variacional". The survey entry calques "take a survey" as "toma esta breve encuesta". The link text "Link to survey" in [61] was left in English.

examples.source: [Variational Quantum Eigensolver (VQE)]
examples.translation: [Eigensolver Cuántico Variacional (VQE)]
examples.suggested: [solucionador propio cuántico variacional (VQE)] or simply keep the English name with VQE
examples.why: This mixes an English noun with Spanish adjectives in title case. A Spanish technical writer would either translate the whole name or keep the English one.

examples.source: Please take this short survey to provide feedback
examples.translation: Por favor, toma esta breve encuesta para proporcionar comentarios
examples.suggested: Responde esta breve encuesta para darnos tu opinión
examples.why: "Tomar una encuesta" is a calque of the English "take a survey". The natural verb in Spanish is "responder" or "contestar".

examples.source: [Link to survey](...)
examples.translation: [Link to survey](...)
examples.suggested: [Enlace a la encuesta](...)
examples.why: This visible link text was left in English on a Spanish page.

editor_note: Meaning holds throughout, including the harder passages: the bias and overhead trade-off in [7]/[136], the timeout caveat in [86], the plain-PEC vs PEC+SLC comparison in [149]-[151], and the Z/X commutation claims in [109]-[110]. Nothing would mislead a learner. The problems are terminology inconsistency. "Bound" switches between "límite" (most entries) and "cota" ([67], [73], [86]), and "límite" is also used for "limit" in "límites de velocidad cuántica" and "tiempo límite". "Gate" is "compuertas" in [15] but "puertas" everywhere else, and "timeout" is "tiempo de espera" in [86] but "tiempo límite" in [92]/[101]. There are also a few calques, such as "localmente consciente" and "no logra conmutar", and "postselección" [9] vs "post-selección" elsewhere.

examples.source: The computed shades are upper bounds at every stage, so hitting the timeout only makes the bounds looser
examples.translation: Las sombras calculadas son cotas superiores en cada etapa, por lo que alcanzar el tiempo de espera solo hace que las cotas sean más laxas
examples.suggested: Pick one term for 'bound' across the file (preferably 'cota', which keeps it separate from 'límite de velocidad' and 'tiempo límite'), and use 'tiempo límite' for 'timeout' as in [92] and [101].
examples.why: 'Bound' is 'cota' here but 'límite' in [78]-[85], [115] and elsewhere, and 'timeout' is 'tiempo de espera' here but 'tiempo límite' in [92]/[101]. A learner may think these are different concepts.

examples.source: cancels out the noise by applying single-qubit gates
examples.translation: cancela el ruido aplicando compuertas de un solo qubit
examples.suggested: cancela el ruido aplicando puertas de un solo qubit
examples.why: Every other entry uses 'puertas' for gate, so this one use of 'compuertas' breaks the file's convention.

examples.source: implementing locally-aware error mitigation
examples.translation: implementar mitigación de errores localmente consciente
examples.suggested: implementar una mitigación de errores que tenga en cuenta la localidad
examples.why: 'Localmente consciente' is a literal calque of 'locally-aware'. A native technical writer would rephrase it.

examples.source: does a Z error fail to commute, while an X error does commute
examples.translation: un error Z no logra conmutar, mientras que un error X sí conmuta
examples.suggested: un error Z no conmuta, mientras que un error X sí lo hace
examples.why: 'No logra conmutar' calques 'fail to' and reads as if the error were trying to commute. Plain 'no conmuta' is the natural phrasing.

examples.source: it is highly beneficial for the deepest learning depth to match the depth of the circuit
examples.translation: resulta muy beneficioso que la profundidad de aprendizaje más profunda coincida con la profundidad del circuito
examples.suggested: resulta muy beneficioso que la mayor profundidad de aprendizaje coincida con la profundidad del circuito
examples.why: 'Profundidad ... más profunda' is a redundant, stiff calque. 'La mayor profundidad' reads naturally.

editor_note: The meaning is faithful throughout, including the hedges in [108], [118], [119] and [122] and the PNA/TREX/PS comparison in [149]-[153]. Nothing here would mislead a learner. 'Expectation value' is split in two: the calque 'valor(es) de expectativa' is used through [0]-[33], then the conventional 'valor esperado' from [142] on. Use 'valor esperado' throughout. 'Left-dressed' in [88] is misread as 'se dejan vestidas', meaning the gates stay dressed, when it means they are dressed on the left of the box. Also, 'primitiva' in [0] becomes 'el primitivo' in [155], 'edge-based' in [104] is 'basada en bordes' instead of 'aristas', and 'conecta la brecha' in [73] is a calque of 'bridges the gap'.

examples.source: Improve expectation values with propagated noise absorption (PNA)
examples.translation: Mejora los valores de expectativa con la absorción de ruido propagado (PNA)
examples.suggested: Mejora los valores esperados con la absorción de ruido propagado (PNA)
examples.why: 'Valor de expectativa' is a calque. The file itself switches to the standard 'valor esperado' from [142] on, so the term is inconsistent.

examples.source: Single-qubit gates are left-dressed within the boxes.
examples.translation: Las puertas de un solo qubit se dejan vestidas (left-dressed) dentro de las cajas.
examples.suggested: Las puertas de un solo qubit se absorben por la izquierda (left-dressed) dentro de las cajas.
examples.why: 'Left' here means the left side of the box, not 'left' as in 'remain'. The Spanish loses which side gets dressed. Keeping the English term in parentheses lessens the harm.

examples.source: Combine error mitigation options with the Estimator primitive
examples.translation: Combina las opciones de mitigación de errores con el primitivo Estimator
examples.suggested: Combinar opciones de mitigación de errores con la primitiva Estimator
examples.why: Everywhere else the file uses the feminine 'la primitiva', and [13] gives this same link title as 'Combinar ... con la primitiva Estimator'.

examples.source: Enables edge-based post-selection using `rx` gates
examples.translation: Habilita la post-selección basada en bordes usando puertas `rx`
examples.suggested: Habilita la post-selección basada en aristas usando puertas `rx`
examples.why: In a coupling-graph context, 'edge' is 'arista'. 'Borde' means a physical boundary.

examples.source: this step bridges the gap between an idealized mirrored circuit and a hardware-ready circuit
examples.translation: este paso conecta la brecha entre un circuito en espejo idealizado y un circuito listo para hardware
examples.suggested: este paso cierra la brecha entre un circuito en espejo idealizado y un circuito listo para hardware
examples.why: 'Conecta la brecha' is a literal calque. The idiomatic Spanish is 'cierra la brecha' or 'tiende un puente'.

editor_note: The meaning is faithful all the way through. Caveats survive, including MEM being unable to change mid-circuit results already used in feedforward, the non-FC-DD labeling warning and the Figure 2a differences. Core terms are consistent: medición intermedia del circuito, retroalimentación, desacoplamiento dinámico, disposición, en bruto. The remaining slips are small. "921,600 shots" keeps the English thousands separator, which reads as a decimal in es-ES. "Feature" is rendered as "función", which collides with "función Orbit" and Qiskit Function. "For fun" is calqued as "Por diversión", "the reverse of" as "el reverso de", and "not readout-mitigated" as "no están mitigadas por lectura". "Bitstrings" [31] alternates with "cadena de bits" [49].

examples.source: for 900 PUBs and 921,600 shots in total
examples.translation: para un total de 900 PUB y 921,600 shots
examples.suggested: para un total de 900 PUB y 921 600 shots
examples.why: In es-ES the comma is the decimal separator, so 921,600 can read as 921.6. A thin space avoids that.

examples.source: Dynamic circuits are presently an experimental feature
examples.translation: Los circuitos dinámicos son actualmente una función experimental
examples.suggested: Los circuitos dinámicos son actualmente una funcionalidad experimental
examples.why: 'función' collides with 'función Orbit' and Qiskit Function on the same page. 'funcionalidad' or 'característica' is clearer.

examples.source: For fun, make sure to compare these results to your results at the end
examples.translation: Por diversión, asegúrate de comparar estos resultados con los tuyos al final
examples.suggested: Como curiosidad, compara al final estos resultados con los tuyos
examples.why: 'Por diversión' is a literal calque that no native technical writer would use.

examples.source: the expected measured string the reverse of the zero-padded binary representation of $x$
examples.translation: que la cadena medida esperada sea el reverso de la representación binaria rellenada con ceros de $x$
examples.suggested: que la cadena medida esperada sea la inversa de la representación binaria de $x$ rellenada con ceros
examples.why: 'el reverso' means the back side of an object. The idiomatic term is 'la inversa' or 'el orden inverso'.

examples.source: its raw curves are not readout-mitigated
examples.translation: sus curvas en bruto no están mitigadas por lectura
examples.suggested: sus curvas en bruto no incluyen mitigación de errores de lectura
examples.why: 'mitigadas por lectura' reads as if the readout does the mitigating. The source means readout errors were not mitigated.

editor_note: The meaning is faithful all the way through. The cubic/quadratic/linear HOBO vs QUBO claim, the CPLEX/Gurobi validation, the random-sampling "fuerza bruta" comparison and the "lower values indicate better solutions" conclusion all match the English. Terminology is consistent (qubits, estado fundamental, vidrio de espín de Ising, cadena de bits, supresión de errores). One register slip breaks the tú convention: "Su tiempo de ejecución puede variar" in [5]. There are also a few calques a native editor would smooth out: "Este tutorial demuestra" / "El ejemplo demostrado" in [7], and "Antecedentes" for "Background" in [6].

examples.source: Your runtime might vary.
examples.translation: Su tiempo de ejecución puede variar.
examples.suggested: Tu tiempo de ejecución puede variar.
examples.why: Formal 'Su' breaks the informal tú convention used everywhere else on the page (asegúrate, consulta, importa).

examples.source: This tutorial demonstrates how to solve... The example demonstrated in this tutorial is...
examples.translation: Este tutorial demuestra cómo resolver... El ejemplo demostrado en este tutorial es...
examples.suggested: Este tutorial muestra cómo resolver... El ejemplo de este tutorial es...
examples.why: 'Demostrar' in Spanish leans toward 'prove', so this is a calque of 'demonstrate'. 'Mostrar', or just dropping the participle, reads more natively.

examples.source: Background
examples.translation: Antecedentes
examples.suggested: Contexto
examples.why: In tutorial section headings, 'Contexto' is the more idiomatic rendering of 'Background'. 'Antecedentes' sounds legal or historical.

editor_note: Both rewritten license entries are faithful and keep the informal tú: [122] "Esto está licenciado bajo la Apache License, Version 2.0. Puedes obtener una copia..." and [123] "debe conservar este aviso de copyright... un aviso que indique que han sido alterados con respecto a los originales".
